customDescriptions.value: Check whether a control function is currently permitted by the FIM — use before executing safety-relevant actuator commands to respect inhibition conditions
Look up a 1-D calibration curve (breakpoints + values) — use for simple characteristic lines like sensor transfer functions or temperature-dependent parameters
Interpolate a 1-D curve using pre-computed index and fraction — use when multiple curves share the same axis breakpoints and you want to compute the prelookup only once
Inject a diagnostic event status into the DEM for testing — use to simulate fault conditions during MIL/SIL validation without triggering real diagnostic monitors
Override the reported status of a diagnostic event in the DEM — use to suppress or force fault states during calibration or integration testing
Provide a complete DEM service interface as a single component — use when modeling a diagnostic manager that processes multiple fault events and reports status to the DCM
Query whether a specific diagnostic event is available in the DEM — use as a guard before calling diagnostic monitor or info services to avoid runtime errors
Retrieve status information about a diagnostic event from the DEM — use to read fault status (tested, confirmed, pending) for downstream decision logic
Report a pass or fail result for a diagnostic event to the DEM — use inside monitor runnables to set fault detected/not-detected based on measured signals
Control operation cycle state in the DEM (start, restart, end) — use to signal driving cycle boundaries that gate when diagnostic debouncing qualifies faults
Internal event listener that triggers the initialization logic — responds to the initialize event to run startup computations
Receive asynchronous events from other AUTOSAR software components — use for inter-runnable triggered communication where data arrives on-demand rather than periodically
Send asynchronous events to other AUTOSAR software components — use to trigger runnables or notify subscribers of state changes
Request inhibition or release of a function through the FIM — use to disable degraded features when prerequisite diagnostic events indicate a fault
Look up a 2-D calibration map (two breakpoint axes + table values) — use for characteristic maps such as base fuel injection or ignition timing vs. speed and load
Interpolate a 2-D map using pre-computed index and fraction inputs — use when multiple maps share axes and you want to reuse a single prelookup computation for efficiency
Provide a complete NvM service interface as a single component — use when modeling persistent storage logic that reads/writes calibration or adaptation data across ignition cycles
Perform administrative NvM operations (set block protection, invalidate, erase) — use for service routines that manage NVRAM block lifecycle beyond normal read/write
Read or write a persistent data block through the NvM service — use to store adaptation values, DTCs, or learned parameters that must survive power cycles
Compute index and fraction from breakpoint data for downstream interpolation blocks — use to share one axis search across multiple Curve/Map Using Prelookup blocks
Generate a ramp signal with configurable slope and initial value — use for rate-limited transitions in actuator commands or soft-start/soft-stop profiles in AUTOSAR MFL functions
Mark a signal as invalid to indicate communication failure or data unavailability — use in sender-receiver interfaces to propagate signal quality status to receiving components
Interpolate a single output value from a calibration axis without prelookup — use for simple 1-D calibration tables where AUTOSAR fixed-point compliance is required
Internal initialization subsystem for the Ramp block — executes once at startup to set the initial state of the ramp generator
Internal constant block providing the initial state value for the Ramp initialization function
Internal data store read for accessing the Ramp persistent state during initialization
Internal data store write for setting the Ramp persistent state during initialization
